Q: 400 Bad Request' when sending media template A:

I ran into the same issue and it turned out not to be related to the n8n workflow, templates, or credentials at all.

The problem was that the WhatsApp phone number was still in Pending state. While the number is pending, WhatsApp Cloud API will return a 400 error (Account not registered) even though the credentials work and the templates are visible.

You don’t need to manually upload or manage any certificate. Once you finish verifying the phone number, WhatsApp handles the certificate automatically in the background.

The verification needs to be completed here:

Business Manager → WhatsApp Manager → Phone Numbers

(not from the Meta App dashboard).

After completing the SMS/voice verification and once the number status changes to Active / Connected, sending templates works without changing anything in n8n.

Q: Why are digits not recognized with pytesseract in clean images A:

Image size

Tesseract OCR works best on character images that are approximately 30 pixels or 40 pixels square. Consider transforming your image so it is a little smaller.

Median filter

You mentioned there is a little bit of noise. I recommend that you take three screen grabs in close succession. By hypothesis they all display the same digits, though with slight variations in background noise. At each pixel location, compute the median value, not the mean. Give the results to OCR.

Thresholding

Consider picking a threshold value and then feeding a black-and-white version of your grayscale to OCR.

Or let Otsu‘s method dynamically pick an appropriate threshold.

Q: How do I turn on word wrap for Output View in VS code? A:

For the editor and notebook output:

"editor.wordWrap": "on",
"notebook.output.wordWrap": true

Q: How can I make VS Code's Source Control View only show changed files and nothing else? A:

You don't need to edit settings.json to only show changed files:

  1. Open the Source Control view

  2. Locate the "..." (ellipsis) menu in the top-right corner of the CHANGES pane title bar.

  3. Click the "..." menu to open the options dropdown.

  4. Navigate to View & Sort.

  5. Select View as Tree.

However, this solution will display the commit buttons, text message text field, and repo names

Q: How to initialize a two-dimensional array (list of lists, if not using NumPy) in Python? A:

Surprisingly haven't seen the itertools option. This is nice because you can cleanly define the dimensions and default value. generation is less legible.

import itertools

rows, cols = 3, 4
value = 0

# Create an iterator that repeats a list of zeros, then zip it to create separate row objects
matrix = list(zip(*itertools.repeat([value] * rows, cols)))

Q: Gmail App search criteria A:

GmailApp.search doesn't support regular expressions. The parameter should be a JavaScript string using Gmail search operators like in:, label:, -, etc. For the complete list of Gmail search operators, see Refine searches in Gmail.

Considering the above, as the GmailApp.search parameter instead of

"user@domain  from:/mail delivery/ || /postmaster/ ||/Undeliverable/ "

use

'user@domain  from:("mail delivery" | "postmaster" | "Undeliverable" )'

If you insist on using regular expressions, you should craft a script that retrieves all threads, then, for each thread, retrieves all messages, and then, for each message, retrieves its body. Once the script has the body, it should use String.prototype.search or another JavaScript String method that supports regular expressions.
